title: How Far Employer Allowance Reaches on Each Employee Meal Account Plan
content:
Allowance granted to an Employee Meal Account is spendable only within the reach the plan prints for it: at so many meal periods a day, for so much of an eligible till transaction, up to a ceiling on one transaction, at named outlets, and combining with published discounts on a named basis.

| Meal plan | Meal periods a day at which allowance may be spent | Share of an eligible till transaction | Ceiling on allowance applied to one transaction | Where allowance may be spent | Allowance and published discounts combine as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account | 0 | 0 percent | $0.00 | the cafe counter only | whichever of allowance and published discount leaves the employee paying less |
| Prepaid Declining Balance Account | 0 | 0 percent | $0.00 | the cafe counter only | whichever of allowance and published discount leaves the employee paying less |
| Payroll Deduction Meal Account | 0 | 0 percent | $0.00 | the cafe counter only | allowance first, published discount against what remains |
| Subsidized Daily Allowance Account | 2 | 100 percent | $9.50 | the cafe counter and the micro market | allowance first, published discount against what remains |
| Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account | 3 | 100 percent | $12.00 | the cafe counter and the micro market | allowance first, published discount against what remains |
| Executive Dining Charge Account | 3 | 100 percent | $95.00 | every outlet at the site | the published discount first, allowance against what remains |

## What the five columns fix

The first is the number of meal periods each day at which allowance may be spent, as a whole number. The second is the share of an eligible till transaction allowance may meet, as a percentage. The third is the ceiling on allowance applied to a single till transaction. The fourth is where allowance may be spent, printed as the cafe counter only, the cafe counter and the micro market, or every outlet at the site. The fifth is how employer allowance and published discounts combine.

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical figures)

On the Subsidized Daily Allowance Account, allowance meets 100 percent of an eligible ticket but no more than $9.50 of one transaction, so a $9.50 eligible ticket is met in full and a $12.00 eligible ticket draws $9.50. On the Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account the share is also 100 percent but the transaction ceiling is $12.00, and allowance there may be spent at 3 meal periods a day rather than 2. The Executive Dining Charge Account carries a $95.00 transaction ceiling and reaches every outlet at the site.

Against the three plans that carry no allowance, these columns print 0 meal periods, 0 percent, $0.00 and the cafe counter only, and their stacking basis is the better of allowance and published discount, which on those plans decides nothing.
